questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Central African Republic about 622,984 square kilometres; Cameroon about 475,442 square kilometres; Israel about 20,770 square kilometres; Palestine about 6,020 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Central African Republic?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Central African Republic article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Central African Republic?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Central African Republic on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Central African Republic article.

questions.proof: It is bordered by the countries of Cameroon, Chad, Sudan, South Sudan, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Republic of the Congo.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Central African Republic?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Central African Republic is the Central African CFA franc.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Bangui?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Central African Republic is Bangui.

source.name: Simple English Wikipedia: Central African Republic
